1d921be7bfe0e25e6765d48f1fe96327.description:
This is a forward-deployed role: you'll work directly with government and defense customers at key points in a project's lifecycle — discovery, feedback sessions, and post-launch — representing design in the room and building the trust needed to get stakeholder buy-in without a manager present.
Own end-to-end design — from ambiguous, undefined requirements through wireframes, high-fidelity mockups, and interactive prototypes — for a customer-facing government/defense product experience.
Partner directly with Product as a peer from the earliest stages of a project, not just at handoff.
Work forward-deployed with customers, building direct relationships during key project touch points (discovery, feedback, post-launch) and confidently socializing design decisions with stakeholders.
Design for complex, data-dense workflows: dashboards, mapping interfaces, alerting systems, and analytical reporting tools.
Work directly in code alongside engineers, going beyond static mockups to help build and refine the shipped experience.
Contribute design assets and interaction patterns back to the broader platform, not just the account or project you're staffed on.
Help calibrate and grow the design team by participating in portfolio reviews and interviews as we scale this function.
Navigate high ambiguity — customer requirements are often not clean or fully defined, and you'll need to help define them.
Influence stakeholders cross-functionally and up to leadership level to align on design direction.
Qualifications
10–15 years of experience across a range of design settings and problem types.
Experience owning end-to-end B2B or enterprise product experiences at a senior/staff level.
Comfortable working with high ambiguity and evolving requirements, typical of early-stage government/enterprise engagements.
Experience designing complex workflow UI, dashboards, or data-heavy/mapping interfaces — whether in government/defense, health tech, fintech, or other high-complexity/high-compliance domains.
Strong client-facing presence — confident presenting to and winning over senior stakeholders, whether in person or remote.
Working understanding of front-end development and how to hand off clean, implementable designs; comfort collaborating directly with engineers on code.
Willingness to travel to customer sites at key project milestones.
Experience in a client-facing role where you presented directly to senior stakeholders.
Exposure to AI/ML tools and fluency using AI in your own design workflow.
Experience contributing to a design system or shared interaction patterns across multiple products or teams.

22e16d73b26c44481649f7bd57a34ae9.description:
About the Team
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Identity team builds the foundational systems that enable people, organizations, devices, and agents to securely access OpenAI products.
The team works across consumer and enterprise experiences, including account structures, sign-in, authentication, recovery, privacy, permissions, administration, and agent identity. As AI systems become increasingly capable of acting on behalf of people and organizations, we are defining new models for authorization and trust across human-to-agent and agent-to-agent interactions.
About the Role
In this role, you’ll lead design for foundational identity experiences across OpenAI’s products. You’ll make permissions, access, risk, and administration feel clear, safe, and genuinely usable—whether someone is securing a personal account, administering access across an enterprise, signing in to another product with ChatGPT, or authorizing an agent to perform sensitive work.
Your work will span established identity challenges and emerging interaction models without established design conventions. You’ll help define how users understand what an agent can access, who or what it is acting on behalf of, and when confirmation or stronger authentication should appear. Working closely with product, engineering, security, privacy, and design, you’ll translate complex policies and technical systems into coherent, trustworthy experiences.
This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.
In this role, you will:
Lead the design direction for identity, account security, permissions, and administrative experiences across OpenAI’s consumer and enterprise products.

Design and ship high-quality experiences spanning sign-in, authentication, account recovery, device accounts, privacy, access controls, governance, and remediation.

Define mental models and interaction patterns for human-to-agent and agent-to-agent identity, authorization, and trust.

Help users understand what people, systems, and agents can access or do on their behalf.

Design security checks and confirmation flows that protect sensitive actions while minimizing unnecessary friction.

Partner closely with product management, engineering, security, privacy, and design peers to shape strategy, roadmap, and execution.

Navigate complex roles, policies, dependencies, and product states to create systems that remain coherent as they scale.

Contribute to and evolve the design systems and patterns used across OpenAI’s identity experiences.

You might thrive in this role if you:
Are a systems-oriented product thinker who can reason across complex states, dependencies, policies, and user types.

Have designed role-based access or permissions for organizations with multiple teams, resources, or levels of administration.

Understand how to balance security, usability, and business needs in high-stakes workflows.

Have strong UX/UI and interaction design skills, with a high bar for contemporary craft, clarity, and quality.

Can turn complicated technical capabilities and policies into mental models that users can understand and trust.

Are comfortable shaping direction when both the underlying technology and established user expectations are evolving.

Have experience with enterprise, platform, desktop, infrastructure, or similarly complex product environments.

Are excited to establish new conventions for identity and access in a world where AI agents increasingly act on behalf of people and organizations.

About OpenAI
OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. d4c19212080d671d7936e008ae7465b1.description:
We are seeking a Product Designer to join our Design Systems (Figma Pattern Library) team, dedicated to building and evolving shared patterns and components across Figma’s expanding suite of products. This role will focus on a consistent and approachable experience for Figma’s audience, regardless of the product they are using. As Figma continues to grow, a cohesive design system that spans multiple products is critical. We are looking for a designer with experience in multi-product environments who can work collaboratively across teams to develop, refine, and implement design systems that scale.
This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.
What you'll do at Figma:
Contribute to the overall strategy and decision-making regarding cross-product design systems.
Define and communicate a clear vision for shared design patterns that can be utilized across various products.
Collaborate with product management, engineering, and other design teams to ensure consistent implementation of design components.
Create, iterate, and refine design system components, including flows, prototypes, and high-fidelity visuals.
Drive the adoption and continuous improvement of the design system across the organization.
5+ years of experience as a Design Systems designer
Experience working independently and collaboratively to explore design solutions from concept to implementation.
Proven ability to create simple, scalable solutions for complex user experiences across multiple products.
Experience managing complex projects that involve collaboration across different teams and organizational boundaries.
Proficiency building concepts in code and using production quality concepts to communicate design decisions effectively.
While it’s not required, it’s an added plus if you also have:
A passion for creating inclusive, user-friendly designs that cater to a broad audience.
Experience mentoring junior or early-career designers.

At Blueprint, you’ll work alongside talented people with different experiences, expertise, and perspectives. You’ll have opportunities to take on meaningful challenges, expand your skills, and see the impact of what you build.
Bring your perspective. Raise the standard. Build what matters.
About the Role
We’re looking for a UX Researcher to help shape AI-powered productivity experiences used by a broad and diverse customer base. In this role, you’ll plan and lead research that uncovers user needs, evaluates product experiences, and informs meaningful product decisions.
You’ll own studies from planning through final presentation, combining qualitative and quantitative methods to turn complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations. You’ll collaborate closely with product managers, designers, engineers, researchers, and other partners throughout the product development lifecycle.
What You'll Do
Plan, design, and conduct end-to-end user research studies using qualitative and quantitative methods.
Identify research questions and select the most effective methods for addressing them.
Conduct usability studies, user interviews, surveys, benchmark studies, and unmoderated research.
Analyze research findings and translate them into clear insights and actionable product recommendations.
Present findings to cross-functional stakeholders and help teams apply the insights to product decisions.
Collaborate with product managers, designers, engineers, researchers, and other partners throughout the product development lifecycle.
Evaluate product experiences and identify opportunities to improve usability, accessibility, and customer satisfaction.
Conduct competitive research to understand industry trends, user expectations, and product positioning.
Use AI tools to support research workflows while critically evaluating outputs and maintaining research quality.
Manage multiple research projects and deliver high-quality findings within accelerated timelines.
Bachelor’s degree in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Computer Science, Human Factors, Cognitive Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
1 to 2 years of experience conducting UX, usability, or product research.
Experience applying both qualitative and quantitative research methods.
Experience planning and managing research projects from initial scoping through analysis and reporting.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate research findings into clear, actionable recommendations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting findings to stakeholders.
Ability to independently manage research activities while collaborating effectively across teams.
Strong organizational and time-management skills in a fast-moving environment.
Experience using AI tools to support research workflows and the judgment to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree or PhD in Human-Computer Interaction, Psychology, Computer Science, Human Factors, Cognitive Science, or a related field.
Experience conducting UX benchmark studies or usability benchmarking.
Experience researching AI-powered products or intelligent user experiences.
Familiarity with usability metrics, customer-satisfaction measurement, and competitive analysis.
Experience working in agile product-development environments with rapid research cycles.
Ability to independently lead research studies from planning through final presentation within short timelines.
Experience communicating complex research findings to technical and nontechnical audiences.
Curiosity, adaptability, and a commitment to learning new research methods and technologies.
A passion for improving customer experiences through evidence-based decision-making.

With an exceptional efficacy rate, the world has taken notice — we've raised over $13M in venture capital, garnered interest from leading neuroscientists and athletes, and established ourselves as the industry's leading brand. Now, we're looking for incredible people to help us share the gift of enhanced cognitive function with the world. If you're looking to be a part of a movement — one that involves both immense self-growth and an ambitious mission to pioneer an industry — we'd love to have you on the team.
About The Role
Our site is our storefront, our salesperson, and our most important brand asset. This is the person who will own the visual identity of that world.
This is first and foremost a digital product design role for someone who likes to see an idea all the way through, from the first concept to the version that goes live. You'd take work from wireframe to full-fidelity, on-brand execution, and use AI tooling to help get it shipped. Experience in ecommerce, direct response, and CRO matters here, particularly building landing pages, checkouts, and commerce-driven UX. Ideally you have real design chops and a point of view on typography, hierarchy, and brand systems, plus a marketer's instinct for what converts. You're as excited talking about a wordmark's clear space as you are about a hypothesis of why a test did or didn't win.
Our brand foundations already exist, so this isn't a reinvention project. It's about extending and applying them with precision and speed across every digital surface: landing pages, PDPs, quiz and onboarding flows, and the design system underneath it all. You'd be the primary thought partner to our Digital Product Manager, and together you'd own both how the work looks and how it performs. Working together you are the conversion layer to the business.
We're also an AI-forward company, and AI fluency genuinely matters in this role. Our team builds custom AI tools for QA, analysis, and reporting, and we'd love a design partner with that same instinct: building interactive prototypes with AI tools instead of relying only on static comps, exploring concept directions in hours instead of days, and knowing where generated output still needs a human hand. Our brands live on craft and our category is regulated, so taste and judgment matter as much as speed.
Own design end to end across Stasis and Thesis digital surfaces, from wireframe through production-ready design, developer handoff, and launch QA.
Partner with our Digital Product Manager to co-own the CRO and experimentation program, from hypothesis and variant through design, launch planning, QA, and readout.
Translate our brand identity into digital execution, and build the design system that makes every future page faster and more consistent to ship.
Design direct response assets that convert, including advertorials, landing pages, offer and pricing modules, and quiz flows, with a clear grasp of the funnel each one serves.
Turn clinical results, ingredient mechanisms, and study data into charts, comparisons, and infographics that are accurate, on-brand, and persuasive at a glance.
Use data as a design input. Session recordings, heatmaps, and test results are where the best hypotheses tend to come from, and we'd love for you to bring your own.
Help shape how our team uses AI in creative and technical work, sharing tools and workflows with the rest of marketing, including a clear eye for where AI isn't the right answer.

7025da2f10c4d646d8000f8ff9cdce76.title: Product Designer
7025da2f10c4d646d8000f8ff9cdce76.description:
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Design at Anthropic sits at the intersection of craft, research, and product intuition. We're a small team working on products that millions of people use daily—and on interactions that don't have established conventions yet.
Our work shapes how people experience AI: whether Claude feels like a tool or a collaborator, whether it earns trust or erodes it. We partner closely with engineers and researchers, often designing around capabilities that are emerging in real-time. That means staying close to the models, prototyping rapidly, and being comfortable with ambiguity.
We care deeply about craft—the details that make something feel polished and trustworthy—but we ship fast and learn in the open. We'd rather get something in front of users and iterate than wait for perfection.
This role is a mix of team leadership and hands-on design execution. As a designer, we're looking for someone who ships fast and stays in motion—you'd rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month. You're excited to question fundamental UI assumptions and invent patterns that feel native to AI, you're already using tools like Claude Code to extend what you can build, and you pay attention to where model capabilities are heading, not just what Claude can do today—all while keeping care for the pixels, the copy, and the edge cases.
As a leader, you develop talent: you've mentored designers and helped them grow their skills, confidence, and impact, and you give clear, actionable feedback. You build alignment without authority, influencing cross-functional partners through strong communication and collaborative problem-solving rather than hierarchy. You know when to roll up your sleeves and when to empower your team—modeling the quality bar while creating opportunities for others to lead. You think systematically, establishing reusable frameworks that help the team work more effectively, and you advocate strategically, representing design in leadership discussions and helping shape product direction rather than just executing on it.

cbb0e8fe50ba2b5f3f64f20d54a1edfd.description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car, a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton, Lady Gaga’s Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe, we encounter exceptional objects every day.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

Taking ownership and driving impact

Being open to change and feedback

Being passionate about our mission and our customers.

Your mission

Great product decisions start with understanding our customers.

As a UX Research Intern in Demand, you will help us better understand how buyers experience Catawiki across the full journey, from discovering interesting objects and deciding whether to participate, to returning and engaging with new experiences over time.

You will support research across a range of buyer topics and product areas, including new experiences such as Catawiki Live. The exact research questions will evolve as our product and customer priorities develop.

You will work closely with UX Research, Product, Design, Engineering and Data teams, helping turn customer behaviour, motivations and pain points into insights that influence real product decisions.

This is a hands on internship. You will learn by doing, contributing across the research process from defining questions and choosing methods through recruitment, facilitation, analysis and communication of findings.

What you will do

Support qualitative and quantitative research across the buyer journey

Plan and conduct interviews, usability tests, surveys and other research studies

Help define research questions and select the right methods to answer them

Support participant recruitment, research materials and session facilitation

Analyse findings and translate them into clear insights and recommendations

Work closely with Product and Design teams to ensure research informs product decisions

Partner with external research providers when needed

Organise and synthesise existing research so teams can more easily reuse previous insights

Help make customer insights visible and accessible across the organisation

Develop practical experience combining qualitative research with behavioural and quantitative data

Who you are

Three qualities matter most in this internship.

Curiosity about people

You want to understand why people behave the way they do and are interested in uncovering the motivations behind what customers say and do.

Research mindset

You approach questions systematically, care about evidence and are interested in learning how different research methods can be used to make better product decisions.

Clear communication

You can listen carefully, identify the important themes and communicate findings in a way that others can understand and act on.

You will also bring:

Enrollment at a Dutch university throughout the full internship period

Availability for a full time six month internship starting in September or October 2026

A strong interest in user experience and customer research

Some experience with qualitative or quantitative research through university, a thesis, previous work or another relevant project

An interest in methods such as interviews, usability testing, surveys, diary studies and desk research

Currently studying towards a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in psychology, behavioural science, human computer interaction, industrial design or a related field

Where you will be

This internship is based in Amsterdam.

Visible impact

About Gusto

At Gusto, we’re on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

We’re looking for a AI-native Design Systems Designer to join Gusto’s Builder Enablement team — the team responsible for Workbench, Gusto’s internal design system, and for how every designer and engineer at Gusto ships high-quality work with AI assistance.

This role sits at an exciting and genuinely new intersection: deep design systems craft combined with fluency in AI-assisted workflows. You’ll help evolve and maintain Workbench at a pivotal moment — we’re mid-Brand Refresh, actively building AI tooling to improve how builders interact with the system, and expanding how the design system serves LLMs and AI-assisted products as much as it serves human designers. The ideal candidate is a rigorous systems thinker with strong component and token expertise who is excited about using AI tools as a core part of how they work, not just an add-on. We use Figma as a helper tool, but our deliverables are code. The level of this role is similar to/equivalent of a Senior Staff-level.

About the Team:

The Builder Enablement team’s mission is to make high-quality, AI-assisted shipping the default for every builder at Gusto. We own Workbench, Gusto’s design system, but we also own how it gets expressed to AI tools and builders. Our work spans component design and documentation, token architecture, AI tooling (including MCP servers, prompt engineering, and eval systems), and supporting the broader design and engineering org in using the system well.

We’re a small, tight-knit team of designers and engineers embedded within Gusto’s design organization, led by our CDO, Amy Thibodeau. We care deeply about craft, systems thinking, and making complex things feel simple for the people who depend on us.

Product Design at Gusto is made up of over 70 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We’re a cross-functional bunch focused on Design, Research, Writing, Ops and Front-end Development who are always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don’t care a whole lot about swim lanes and we work closely with our partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build and ship experiences that make a difference. We are passionate advocates for thoughtful, crafted, and inclusive experiences and we believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful. Read more about Design at Gusto.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

Design and maintain Workbench components and patterns, including complex components with variables, variants, and tokenized styles

Own and evolve semantic and functional token architecture as we execute the Brand Refresh and move toward theming

Work closely with our engineering team to ensure component consistency including coded implementations — pairing on design decisions, reviewing implementations, contributing to technical plans, and committing your own PRs.

Contribute to AI tooling that helps designers and engineers use Workbench correctly — including struc

6b19860188b83a2cf58610021b6ddffb.description:
An Enterprise Technology Management platform for end-to-end visibility and automation of IT ecosystems.
Enterprise Software It Service Management Logistics Orchestration Cost Optimization Security Enforcement
Job Description
Oomnitza offers the industry’s most versatile Enterprise Technology Management platform that orchestrates and automates key business processes for IT. Our SaaS solution, with agentless integrations, best practices and low-code workflows, enables enterprises to leverage their existing infrastructure systems and automate processes such as offboarding, onboarding, audit readiness, refresh forecasting and more, thereby reducing reliance on error-prone manual tasks and tickets. We help some of the most well-known and innovative companies to improve efficiency, expedite audits, mitigate cyber risk and eliminate redundant IT spend.
Oomnitza is hiring a UX Design Engineer to own the design system, component library, and prototyping tooling that powers our Product Engineering team. In our model, Product Engineers run discovery and prototyping end-to-end; your job is to give them an opinionated, well-tested, well-documented platform so they can move fast without losing design quality.
This is a hands-on role. Most of your time is in code and design tooling: maintaining the system, evolving the Storybook component library, building scaffolding that makes prototyping fast, and consulting on the small number of interactions that are genuinely novel. The role can sit in the US or in Ireland since most of the work is with tooling and systems.
What You’ll Do
Own the Oomnitza design system end-to-end: visual language, interaction patterns, accessibility guardrails, and the rules that keep the product feeling like one product.
Maintain and extend the Storybook component library. Components should be correct, documented, performant, accessible, and easy for Product Engineers to compose.
Build and maintain the prototyping tooling (design tokens, AI-prompt scaffolds, design markdowns, starter kits) that lets Product Engineers move from idea to validated prototype in days.
Consult with Product Engineers on UX interactions that fall outside the patterns, and produce the new pattern, component, or guidance that adds back to the system.
Partner with engineering to keep the design system and the implementation library aligned. Identify when a one-off interaction should be promoted into the system.
Hold the quality bar for design output across the team. Review prototypes against the system, flag drift, and make the right thing easy to do.
Track the design-engineering space (Figma plugins, AI design tooling, headless component libraries, accessibility standards) and propose investments that make the team faster.
Bachelor’s degree in design, human-computer interaction, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
5+ years combined across product design and front-end engineering. You are equally comfortable in Figma and in a modern front-end codebase.
Experience owning or substantially contributing to a production design system and a Storybook or equivalent component library.
Strong front-end skills: React, TypeScript, modern CSS including design tokens, and accessibility best practices.
Comfort with AI-enabled design and prototyping workflows. You see AI as a way to make the design system more useful, not as a replacement for it.
Strong taste paired with the discipline to systematize it. You recognize good design and codify it into reusable patterns and components.
Strong written and verbal communication. You can document a pattern, brief a Product Engineer, and influence without authority.
Self-directed and outcome-oriented. You identify the highest-leverage investments in the system and prioritize without close supervision.
B2B SaaS or enterprise software experience is a strong plus.
Health Insurance for you, your spouse and dependents
Pension, Life insurance and Income protection
A progressive, healthy work cultu

About DualEntry
DualEntry is building the OS for finance.
Every business needs a financial system of record, yet the world's largest fintech market ($220B+) still runs on software from the 1990s. DualEntry's AI-native ERP automates accounting from data entry to close, so finance teams move faster, spend less and incur less risk.
In just 2 years we've raised $100M+ from Lightspeed, Khosla Ventures, Contrary and Google Ventures and earned the trust of customers from $5M ARR to publicly traded companies.
We hire outliers - people who have achieved difficult things, in their careers or beyond. You'll find leaders, colleagues who've competed at the highest levels of sport, performed on Broadway, trained with UFC champions and founded the country’s largest Python community.

Why This Role Matters Now

Where You'll Create Impact
Define how DualEntry shows up in the world. You’ll make decisions that shape perception with CFOs, operators and finance teams: an audience that notices when something feels cheap and responds when something feels considered

Lead dualentry.com as a living expression of the brand. From landing pages and feature pages to campaign moments, you’ll design with an obsessive eye for hierarchy, craft and conversion

Drive the creative for DualEntry’s events presence: CFO dinners, conference booths, sponsored activations. You’ll ensure every physical touchpoint feels as intentional as the digital ones

Build scalable systems, not one-off assets. Deck masters, social frameworks, email layouts, print templates: you’ll create the infrastructure that lets brand quality compound over time

Partner directly with PMM, Marketing, and Sales as a creative strategist. You know how to receive a brief, challenge it when it’s wrong and translate positioning into visual storytelling that lands

What Sets You Up for Success
Hardcore work ethic and high agency

4+ years of design experience in-house at a high-growth B2B SaaS company, a top-tier agency or both. The best candidates will have seen both environments

A portfolio that makes us stop scrolling. Strong work across brand identity, web, print and event or environmental design. Multidisciplinary range is essential. We’re looking for craft and conviction, not volume

You’ve built and evolved brand systems, not just executed within them. You understand the difference between a brand guide and a living identity

You have a point of view about what great B2B brand looks like, and the confidence to defend it. To a CEO, a PMM, or a vendor who wants to take the easy path

You operate at both strategic and executional altitude without losing quality at either end. You can define the system and then execute the asset

You’re fluent in Figma and Adobe Creative Suite. Tools are not a bottleneck for you. Webflow experience is a plus

High agency. You don’t wait to be told what to do next, and you don’t need creative guardrails to do your best work

Why You’ll Thrive Here
Significant equity ownership in one of the top AI companies in the world

You’re joining early and will grow with DualEntry

Your feedback shapes the product directly

High-speed, high-trust environment with high expectations

Meet the team
Jan made sure we were the ones being understood. Owned marketing messaging, positioning, and voice. Redesigned the DualEntry website in her first 90 days. Also launched a bi-coastal NYC/SF campaign covering over 100+ billboards that lifted brand visibility and awareness

Ana took the lead and owned the community and events at DualEntry from end to end. Thousands of attendees across 15+ events in 6 months. Dinners, roundtables, poker night and much more!

PrecisionLender is Q2's relationship pricing and profitability platform trusted by commercial banks and financial institutions to win better deals, grow profitable relationships, and make smarter decisions at the point of negotiation. Our platform combines real-time pricing intelligence, market benchmarking, and AI-assisted guidance to help bankers structure deals that are good for their customers and good for their institution.
What You'll Do Here
As a Product Designer, you'll be part of the Product team, working closely with software engineers, product managers, and product owners. You'll use your expert knowledge of design and user research to find meaningful ways to improve our product and processes.
You'll be empowered to listen to our clients' needs and act on them. Our Product Designers own the end-to-end user experience, including wireframing, feature definition, designing mockups, usability testing, user research, and advocating for a high-quality, accessible product.
The users you'll design for are commercial bankers, relationship managers, administrators, and banking leadership — professionals who work in high-stakes, fast-moving environments where every workflow decision has real business impact. Understanding their world, their constraints, and what it means to win a deal is core to doing this job well.
You'll be instrumental in shaping the direction of the design team — providing meaningful feedback on designs, thinking about the future of design at Q2, collaborating across the product organization, and contributing to strategy, goals, and roadmap conversations.
What People Say About You
You have stellar written and verbal communication skills, and a gift for explaining complicated things simply. You're driven and persistent — you find ways to make processes better, and then you make it happen. Your scrappiness makes you a natural problem solver who doesn't give up when the answers aren't obvious. You have a bias toward action and never walk by a mess without cleaning it up.
If you like diving into complex business requirements to build simple, intuitive workflows — and working with industry experts in finance and software to build a diverse suite of tools — we think you'll find a great home at PrecisionLender. You'll have the resources and the space to continually hone your craft and grow your impact.
Bring Your Passion, Do What You Love. Here’s What We’re Looking For:
You may already have experience working in the financial industry or for a software company, or you may not; what’s most important is your enthusiasm to learn. To be successful in this role, you’ll need to be empathetic, resourceful, and humble.

Lisk is building a new kind of financial platform for businesses - one that brings the best of crypto infrastructure into an experience that feels modern, simple, and built for how teams actually operate. We're replacing fragmented corporate financial tooling with a single workspace across web and mobile.
We're looking for a Product Designer to own the design of meaningful parts of the Lisk product end-to-end - from research and problem framing through flows, high-fidelity UI, launch, and iteration. You'll work across our core surfaces and partner closely with product, engineering, sales, and marketing to ship.
This isn't a role where you inherit a mature design system and polish screens. We're early-stage, which means a lot of customer research still to do - you'll spend real time with users, validate patterns in the open, and turn those learnings into design direction. You'll define foundational UX patterns from first principles, design around a stack with deep third-party integrations, and make calls that shape how businesses move money globally.
Own design areas end-to-end: discovery, problem framing, flows, prototypes, high-fidelity UI, launch, and iteration
Build and maintain the design system - components, patterns, and guidelines that scale across web and mobile
Design complex financial workflows end-to-end, including the states and edge cases most teams skip
Make tight scope and tradeoff calls in close partnership with product and engineering
Design within the capability boundaries of our integration partners, and push back where the experience demands it
Run customer research end-to-end - interviews, usability testing, prototype testing - and turn what you learn into design direction
Define what good looks like for the areas you own and hold the bar on craft
Contribute to product strategy and help shape what gets built next
5+ years of product design experience, with meaningful time spent on complex, multi-surface products (web + mobile)
Proven fintech experience - you've shipped financial products at depth
Strong portfolio showing end-to-end work on complex products, not just finished visuals (required with application)
Experience building or significantly contributing to a design system
Comfort with technically deep product surfaces and heavy third-party integration work
Strong systems thinking - you design in patterns, states, and components, not just happy paths
Sharp judgment on scope, sequencing, and what's actually worth building
Excellent written communication for a remote, async-first team
Ability to work within European timezone and working hours
Motion design, animation, or illustration - craft that goes beyond static UI
Experience designing data-heavy interfaces like dashboards, tables, and charts
Hands-on experience with AI prototyping tools - you enjoy turning an idea into something people can click through
We're a remote-first team spread across the world. Working across time zones pushes us to communicate clearly, keep context open, and move quickly without unnecessary friction. Our working hours center around European time zones. We trust people to take ownership, make decisions, and deliver outcomes - while staying aligned through a mix of real-time teamwork and async communication.
Flexible work schedule so you can balance life and work on your terms
Annual team retreats in amazing locations - not corporate offsites, but trips you'll actually look forward to
You'll be building at the frontier of business finance. That means no playbooks, no best practices, no old ways of doing things. You'll own design from the ground up and help define how businesses interact with money. If you want massive upside and the chance to help create a category that reshapes global finance, this is the place to be.

Apex is looking for an outstanding UX Designer to research and create the future of Octopus, our proprietary operating system for building spacecraft at scale. Octopus is an integrated suite of engineering, manufacturing, and operations software developed entirely in-house — it links inventory management, production scheduling, quality, and assembly work instructions into a single environment that adjusts dynamically to changing demand. You will be responsible for researching, designing, innovating, and prototyping the experiences that technicians, engineers, planners, and operators depend on every day to build satellites in a way that has never been done before.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.
Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. We believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful.
We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers. This isn't a future aspiration — it's how we work now, and it's changing what the design role looks like at Gusto and across the industry.
About the role
Gusto is building the financial platform that small businesses will rely on for the next decade, and AI is at the center of that. From how businesses move money, to how Gusto manages risk and verifies identity, AI is changing what's possible across every part of the experience. The design challenge is defining what it looks like to build those products right: not just faster and smarter, but genuinely trustworthy for the hundreds of thousands of businesses and employees who depend on them.
As the Product Designer, Finance, you'll set the UX vision and strategy across four interconnected product areas: Business Money, Consumer Money, Payments, and Risk. Your role is to see what individual teams can't, identifying opportunities and systemic gaps that span the full financial experience, and to drive the work that makes Gusto's financial products feel clear, trustworthy, and empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and their employees. Nobody has fully figured out what AI-first financial UX looks like at scale. This role is the chance to define it at Gusto. This role's level is similar to Senior Staff.
Your work will span the full scope: defining a long-term UX vision that connects financial and trust experiences across teams, identifying and driving high-impact opportunities that no single pod could tackle alone, and shaping product strategy alongside product directors and engineering leaders. You'll step in as a direct IC on the highest-priority projects, develop other designers, and contribute platform patterns that scale beyond the Money and Risk teams.
The Money team builds the financial products that help small businesses and their employees move, manage, and access money—from the tools owners use to run their business finances, to the financial benefits available to their teams. As Gusto deepens its financial ecosystem, this team sits at the center of making money movement faster, simpler, and more empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and the people who work for them.
The Risk team is the trust layer that makes all of it possible. They build the systems that protect customers and Gusto from fraud and financial exposure, and the identity infrastructure that determines how customers verify who they are and how they access Gusto's financial products. It's foundational work: quiet when it's working, critical when it's not.
Together, these two teams own one of the broadest and most consequential design scopes at Gusto.
Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:
Set the UX vision and strategy across the Money and Risk teams, connecting the dots across multiple pods and ensuring a cohesive experience

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. This role is a hybrid of UX research and research operations: you’ll conduct research, primarily usability and quality-validation testing, and you’ll maintain the social and technical systems that make research at Tailscale repeatable and scalable.
You’ll report to the design manager and work closely with the current UX researcher, who will remain the team’s strategic research lead. Day to day, you’ll also work with product designers, product managers, and engineers across the organization. Initially, you will be focused on handling a backlog of studies, with a heavy focus on one large ongoing project. Over time, you will grow towards owning the research direction for one or more product areas with increasing autonomy.

Initially your work will be more reactive, and dependent on teams that are currently shifting their planning and delivery rhythms, and reorganizing and re-scoping work. Own the full study lifecycle, from recruiting and scoping through analysis, communicating results, and identifying and collaborating on opportunities.
Over time, grow from testing what others identify toward owning the research direction for one or more product areas.
Stakeholder enablement. Product teams are increasingly expected to understand what their users are experiencing and what problems need attention. You’ll support this transition.
Coach designers and PMs through study design, reviewing whether their approach will produce a clear signal, and helping them interpret results and decide on next steps.
Build reusable enablement assets, such as templates, reference guides, research skills and workflows, so that your support scales.
Maintain research infrastructure. As more people run studies and work with research data, the underlying systems need to hold up.
Maintain and improve the research library: standardizing how studies are documented, keeping tags and project organization healthy, ensuring past research is findable and useful.
Manage and maintain the research tool stack, which includes the tools we use, templates and guides, and other resources that enable non-stakeholders to engage with or do some limited research themselves.
Work with staff and other researchers to review continuous feedback and ensure issues and friction points get tracked by the relevant EPD pods.

Handle vendor renewals and procurement coordination, working with legal, finance, and the senior researcher to keep contracts current and paperwork moving.

Develop expertise and deep knowledge in how users find, try, and adopt Tailscale

Job Description
Product development used to mean manually writing code, running analysis, diagnosing bugs, and rolling out changes using dozens of tools.
PostHog is the only platform that acts like a co-pilot for you (and your AI agents) to do it all – autonomously.
We started with open-source product analytics, launched out of Y Combinator’s W20 cohort. We’ve since shipped more than a dozen products, including:
PostHog Code, the only AI devtool that understands your product, not just your codebase.
A built-in data warehouse, so users can query product and customer data together using custom SQL insights.
PostHog AI, an AI-powered analyst that answers product questions, helps users find useful session recordings, and writes custom SQL queries.
Product-led . More than 450,000 organizations have installed PostHog, mostly driven by word-of-mouth. We have intensely strong product-market fit.
Default alive . Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we’re very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.
Well-funded. We’ve raised more than $180m from some of the world’s top investors. We’re set up for a long, ambitious journey.
We’re focused on building an awesome product for end users, hiring exceptional teammates, shipping fast, and being as weird as possible.
Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook. Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.
Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what’s going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions. Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.
Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can’t do that shipping at a normal pace. We’ve built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.
Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We’re a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days, and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you’ve ever had.
Ambition: We want to solve big problems. We strongly believe that aiming for the best possible upside, and sometimes missing, is better than never trying. We’re optimistic about what’s possible and our ability to get there.
Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it’s fun.
The Platform UX team helps developers develop better products for developers by creating a UX that people won’t forget. We’re a small team where you get to work with our own self proclaimed beacon of user-focused-light, Adam Leith
We are looking for a rare breed: a builder who sits at the exact intersection of pixel-perfect design and high-velocity engineering . You aren’t just a “coder”. You are a product owner who uses the latest tools to ship ambitious features faster than most teams think possible.
You are someone who speaks ‘Designer intuition’, understands typography, whitespace, visual hierarchy, and color theory.
You look at a Figma file and see why a 4px shift in padding matters, and you speak Developer Logic: understanding the DOM, component

Episodic/longform cutdowns with cliffhanger endings

Dialogue trailers (twist reveals, villain POV, power-scaling/versus edits, lore drops, fight-choreo montages)

Comment-overlay hook edits

Fan-edit style content (thirst traps, theory breakdowns, trend-driven cuts)

Streamer/reactor-cam reaction overlays

What You’ll Bring:

Proven short-form/vertical video editing experience (TikTok, Reels, Shorts, or similar)

Able to turn around finished edits in 1–3 days

Comfortable working across multiple content formats and styles within the same week

Working knowledge of AI video generation tools (Runway, Kling, Sora, Pika, Luma, etc.) — or a fast learner who’s genuinely excited to pick them up

Strong sense of hook, pacing, and what makes someone stop scrolling in the first 1–2 seconds

Reliable communication and file delivery (Frame.io, Drive, Dropbox, etc.)

Nice To Have:

Background in action, anime, gaming, or superhero content/fandoms

Motion graphics / VFX / After Effects skills

Experience with AI voice, image, or video tools beyond basic prompting

Past work on trailer cuts, dialogue edits, or reaction-style content

$40 - $50 an hour

Salary is determined based on the candidate’s experience, skills, and alignment with the requirements of the role, as well as internal equity and market benchmarks.

Target's Global UX team is a group of design, content, research, and accessibility practitioners and experts, with a passion for improving and innovating our digital experiences for Target's guests, team members, and partners. About the Role:
As a UX Researcher - AI Enablement, you will contribute research that helps Target understand and improve AI-enabled and agentic experiences for technical and product practitioners and other enterprise team members. This individual-contributor role focuses on scoped projects with immediate impact at the project and team level.
You will work with Lead and Director-level researchers, applying established qualitative and quantitative methods to well-defined questions and contributing to larger programs and pilots. With direction and guidance, you will contribute to research planning, conduct straightforward studies, participate in analysis and synthesis, and communicate findings that support product and experience decisions.

Participate in analysis and synthesis, organize evidence, and communicate clear findings to project partners.
Collaborate with cross-functional partners on research methods, measures, and decisions that affect the immediate work.
Contribute evidence to personas, journey maps, service blueprints, and shared research knowledge.
Help test and document responsible AI-enabled research workflows while meeting project goals, constraints, timelines, and quality standards.
Core responsibilities of this job are described within this job description. Job duties may change at any time due to business needs.
About You:
2+ years of relevant UX, product, academic, or applied research experience, or equivalent demonstrated skills.
Working knowledge of qualitative and quantitative research methods and when to use them.
Experience conducting straightforward interviews, usability tests, or similar studies with guidance.
Ability to organize qualitative data and perform basic analysis of simple quantitative data.
Clear communication and collaboration skills with peers and cross-functional partners.
Ability to work independently on well-defined problems, manage assigned work, and meet project deadlines.
Curiosity about AI/ML and willingness to build technical literacy; prior AI experience is helpful but not required .
Commitment to inclusive research, accessibility, participant privacy, ethics, and high-quality craft.

📌 ABOUT ALPACA HEALTH
Alpaca Health helps clinicians become entrepreneurs, starting in autism care. We give BCBAs the software, payer contracting, and back-office muscle to launch and scale their own practices, so power in healthcare shifts back to the people actually giving the care.

We have raised over $14M from investors like Core Innovation Capital, Adverb Ventures, and South Park Commons. We serve hundreds of families and are growing 30% month over month.

We also move fast. Last week we threw a festival for 600 people, planned in under two weeks, with real alpacas on site. That is the energy around here. If that sounds like your kind of chaos, keep reading.

🎯 THE ROLE
We are hiring a UX/UI Designer to own the design of everything a family touches on a screen. That means our marketing website, landing pages, campaign microsites, email, and the whole parent acquisition funnel, plus the product experiences families and providers use once they are in the door. You will work right next to our graphic designer (who owns brand craft and assets) and hand in hand with our product and engineering teams to ship.

Most companies split web and product design across two teams that never talk, so the marketing site and the app end up feeling like two different companies. Not here. You make the entire journey feel like one thing: warm, clear, and a little bit magic. Bold ideas are welcome (an intake that feels like a conversation instead of a form, a landing page that explains autism care to a frightened parent in ten seconds) as long as you can prototype them and ship them.

🚧 WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own the web experience
Design and ship our marketing website, landing pages, and campaign microsites

Design email and lifecycle touchpoints that feel human, not corporate

Own the parent acquisition funnel
Design the end-to-end journey from first click to booked, and optimize it for clarity and conversion

Run experiments, read the data, and keep reducing friction and time to care

Design product UX/UI
Design family-facing and provider-facing flows, screens, and prototypes, in close partnership with our product team and Founding Product Designer

Turn complex healthcare workflows into interfaces that feel genuinely simple

Build one cohesive system
Create and maintain a design system that spans marketing and product so everything feels like one brand

Prototype fast, test with real parents and BCBAs, and iterate on what you learn

Partner and ship
Work directly with engineers to get your designs into production at a high bar, not just into a Figma file

Use AI tools to prototype and move faster

🌟 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE
In 90 days: You have shipped a materially better marketing site or set of key landing pages, mapped and improved the top of the acquisition funnel, and laid the foundation of a shared design system with the graphic designer and product team.

In a year: The whole family journey (ad to landing page to intake to app) feels like one seamless product, conversion and time to care have measurably improved, and there's a design system the team builds on every day.

🧠 WHO YOU ARE
You are a self-starter who does not need a PRD to begin. You find the problem and start designing.

You have genuine taste and understand aesthetics, on both the web and product side.

You are a real hybrid: as strong at conversion-driven web and landing pages as you are at product flows, prototypes, and systems.

You are full of bold ideas and pragmatic enough to prototype and ship them on a real deadline.

You are fluent in Figma, comfortable building and maintaining design systems, and you love working with engineers to get things live.

You talk to users and let real insight and data guide your decisions, not just your gut.

You are AI-native and use modern tools to move faster.

You care about families navigating autism care, and it shows in how carefully you design for them.

✨ BONUS POINTS
Front-end familiarity (HTML and CSS, or tools like Framer or Webf

We’re looking for designers who are obsessive about quality, shipping speed, and impact. Job Description

We’re building a centralised UX Research capability within a FTSE 250 financial services organisation — and this role is a key part of that foundation.

As a midweight UX Researcher, you’ll lead meaningful research that shapes product direction, builds shared confidence, and helps teams make better decisions earlier. You’ll be part of the Advised team while sitting within a growing central UX Research team, giving you both focus and community.

This is a hands-on role for a confident researcher who can independently plan and deliver high-quality discovery research, work closely with designers and product teams, and clearly communicate insight to influence outcomes.

What you’ll do:

Lead generative and tactical discovery research end-to-end — from framing the problem through to insight and recommendations.

Select and apply appropriate research methods to meet research goals, with autonomy and confidence.

Partner closely with UX Designers on tactical discovery, supporting early exploration and shaping ideas before evaluative testing.

Conduct a mix of qualitative and quantitative research, including moderated and unmoderated studies, surveys and in-person observation at adviser firms.

Synthesise research into clear, actionable insights that teams can use immediately.

Present findings and recommendations to stakeholders, tailoring the message to different audiences.

Provide strong evidence to support decision-making, helping teams move forward with confidence.

Contribute to the development of research practices, ways of working, and tooling as the function matures.

What ‘good’ looks like in this role:

You can run discovery research independently and know how to adapt when things change.

You’re comfortable making methodological decisions and explaining why you’ve taken a particular approach.

Stakeholders trust your work and understand the value of research because you communicate it clearly.

Designers see you as a partner, not a handover point.

You’re confident speaking up when evidence challenges assumptions — and you do it constructively.

You help establish thoughtful, pragmatic research practices rather than over-engineering process.

What you’ll bring:

Proven experience working as a UX Researcher, leading studies independently.

Strong grounding in qualitative research, with experience applying quantitative methods where appropriate.

Confidence choosing and applying research methods to answer real product questions.

Experience collaborating with designers and product teams in an agile or iterative environment.

Ability to synthesise complex findings into clear, compelling insight.

Comfortable presenting research outputs to a range of stakeholders.

Experience working in regulated environments or financial services is helpful but not essential.

How we work:

We’re establishing a research culture that values thoughtful execution — doing just enough research to make confident decisions, without slowing teams down. You’ll be encouraged to challenge norms gently, bring strong evidence to the table, and help embed research as a strategic partner rather than a gatekeeper.

You won’t be expected to line-manage in this role, but you will be expected to take ownership of your work and contribute to shaping how research shows up across the organisation.

AJ Bell is one of the UK’s fastest-growing investment platform businesses, providing award-winning solutions for everyone, from professional financial advisers to first-time investors.

Today, over 762,000 customers trust us to manage more than £121.5 billion of assets. By continually striving to make investing simpler and more accessible, we’re helping more people take control of their financial futures.

We’re proud to be recognised as one of the UK’s Best 100 Companies to Work For for six consecutive years, and a Great Place to Work® in 2025 and 2026 a reflection of our supportive and collaborative culture.

25 days hol

50d41c73794a0b5323bac1d6e6eded1b.description:
Rockstar is recruiting for a social platform and virtual world with millions of players around the globe. Identity, self-expression, and play are at the core of everything the company builds. Their players come to the platform to connect, create, and belong, and they spend real time and real care there. The company is profitable and self-funded, has been building for over a decade, and has a small, high-trust team where the work directly shapes an app used by millions of people daily.
The Role
The company is looking for an exceptional product designer to shape how millions of people experience play and friendship every day.
The company doesn't hire on years of experience. They hire on the work. This role fits two kinds of people: a junior designer with rare talent whose portfolio already outclasses most seniors, or a seasoned designer with a stellar track record shipping products used by millions. Either way, the bar on fundamentals is the same: typography, hierarchy, spacing, color, interaction. These can't be faked, and they're the first thing the company looks at.
The designer will own design problems end to end: from understanding the player and the problem, through flows and wireframes, to polished, production-ready UI that ships. They are not handing off to the next person in the pipeline. They are seeing it through to the moment it lands in players' hands, and then they are watching how it lands. The company ships fast, iterates on live feedback from one of the most engaged communities in gaming, and holds everything it releases to a standard its players can feel.
This is a high-output, high-accountability, and high-reward role. If that excites a candidate instead of intimidating them, that's the energy the company is looking for.
Own design work end to end: research, flows, wireframes, prototypes, and final polished UI. Shipped, not just mocked.
Design experiences around play, self-expression, and friendship that feel effortless to millions of players across a deep, complex product.
Build on and strengthen the company's design system: establish patterns where they don't exist, and hold the line on consistency where they do.
Back decisions with evidence: player interviews, usage data, and a sharp study of the best products in and outside of gaming.
Iterate relentlessly on live feedback. Care how the work performs in players' hands, not just how it looks in Figma.
A portfolio that speaks for itself: impeccable visual craft, clear thinking behind every decision, and fundamentals strong enough that they need no explanation.
One of two profiles: an early-career designer whose talent and rate of growth are impossible to ignore, or an experienced designer who has shipped world-class product design at scale. The company cares about the quality of the work, not the length of the résumé.
Real taste, backed by rigor: a strong user-centered point of view, and the research and reasoning to defend it.
The ability to produce exceptional work fast. Speed and quality are both non-negotiable.
Fluency in Figma and modern design tooling. Comfort with AI-assisted workflows is a plus. Whatever gets the designer to the best result, fastest, as long as the taste and final decisions are theirs.
A complete ownership mentality. Find the problems worth solving, drive the work forward, and make everyone around them sharper.
A genuine love of games, social products, or virtual worlds is a strong plus. The best work comes from people who understand why players care.
A profitable, self-funded company that's been building for over a decade
A small, high-trust team where the designer's work directly shapes an app used by millions of people globally every day
The creative freedom, and the responsibility, to do the best work of their career

4cae06a3b547c2059af4da0b7d95310b.description:
This is a high-impact internship for someone who wants genuine influence over what we build, how it works, and how it feels. You won’t be doing busywork, and your work won’t disappear into a concept folder. You’ll help design things that ship.
What You’ll Do
Design polished product experiences across core areas of the Plasiv platform.
Contribute to features end-to-end, from research and workflow mapping to prototyping, high-fidelity design, implementation, and iteration.
Explore AI-native interactions involving recommendations, automation, explainability, system feedback, and human control.
Work closely with the founding product designer, founders, and engineers from the earliest product conversations, not downstream of them.
Use prototypes to think, communicate, test ideas, and move product decisions forward.
Contribute to our design system, component library, visual language, and reusable interaction patterns.
Learn from real customer usage and continue improving experiences after they ship.
You’re currently pursuing or have recently completed a degree in Product Design, HCI, Interaction Design, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
A strong portfolio that shows how you solve difficult UX problems, not only your final screens.
Strong interaction and visual design skills, with proficiency in Figma.
Experience working with design systems, reusable components, variants, and component-based product thinking.
Comfort with code and an understanding of how digital products are built. You don’t need to be a front-end engineer, but code shouldn’t feel like a mysterious black box.
Clear communication and a willingness to share early, receive feedback, and keep improving.
Experience with React, TypeScript, HTML/CSS, Tailwind, or similar frontend technologies.
Previous experience at a startup or on a small, fast-moving product team.
An AI product, technical platform, developer tool, or complex systems project in your portfolio.
Experience prototyping with tools like Cursor, Claude Code, or other AI-assisted building tools.
Skills in motion design, data visualization, information architecture, or user research.
Work arrangement: In-person is strongly preferred
Potential: There may be opportunities to continue working with Plasiv depending on performance and mutual fit
Speed matters at Plasiv because learning matters.
We share work early, test ideas quickly, and improve them as we learn. We care deeply about quality, but we don’t wait for perfect conditions before making progress.
Design, engineering, and product decisions happen together. You’ll be part of the conversations where the product is shaped, working alongside the people building it and the founders setting its direction.
You won’t always receive a neat brief with every answer included. Sometimes you’ll start with a customer problem, a rough idea, or a workflow no one has fully untangled yet. Your job is to ask good questions, make the problem visible, explore possibilities, and help the team find the right answer through making.
We’re ambitious, direct, collaborative, and serious about the work without taking ourselves too seriously.

Great customer support requires human agents and AI in perfect balance, and Assembled is the only unified platform that orchestrates both at scale. Companies like Canva, Etsy, and Robinhood use Assembled to coordinate their entire support operation — in-house agents, BPOs, and AI — in a single operating system. With AI Agents that resolve cases end-to-end, AI Copilot for agent assistance, and AI-powered workforce management that optimizes both human and AI capacity, Assembled helps teams deliver faster, better service while making smarter decisions about how to staff and automate. Backed by $71M from NEA, Emergence Capital, and Stripe, we're building the platform that makes AI and human collaboration actually work.
About the Role
We’re looking for a Product Designer to take on some of the broadest and most complex product problems at Assembled. You’ll design tools that help support teams understand what’s happening across their operations, make high-stakes decisions, plan for the future, and increasingly work alongside AI to get things done.
This is a role for someone excited by making sophisticated software feel remarkably simple. You’ll work across new products, foundational workflows, data-rich experiences, and emerging agentic UX patterns. You’ll help define how people delegate work to AI, understand its decisions, intervene when needed, and stay confidently in control. You’ll have significant ownership: working directly with customers, helping identify the right problems to solve, shaping product strategy, and carrying ideas from early research through polished, shipped experiences.
This is an onsite role based in our New York City office, five days a week (Monday–Friday).
What You'll Do
Turn complex operational workflows into products that feel intuitive, powerful, and approachable.
Define new interaction patterns for working with AI agents, including how users delegate work, understand decisions, and stay in control.
Design data-rich experiences that help customers understand what’s happening, why it matters, and what to do next.
Shape new product areas and foundational workflows, from planning and analytics to setup, configuration, and integrations.
Lead customer research and discovery, translating real operational needs into product strategy and decisions the team can rally around.
Partner deeply with product and engineering to influence the roadmap, prototype quickly, and carry ideas through implementation and launch.
Use AI agents to instrument experiences, prototype ideas, and run experiments—applying the technology we build on to how we build.
3+ years designing and shipping production B2B software, with a pull toward complex, consequential customer problems.
Strong systems and interaction design; you can distill messy, multi-stakeholder needs into clear, reusable experiences.
You turn ambiguity into shipped product quickly, without losing sight of craft or customer impact.
You lead your own research and build close relationships with the people who use what you design.
You're a strong communicator who brings customers, engineers, product partners, and teammates along with your thinking.
You make powerful, data-dense products approachable for non-technical operators without sacrificing depth or flexibility.
You're energized by broad ownership and comfortable influencing both product strategy and execution.
You get into the code and have used coding agents to prototype or ship.
AI fluency in practice (Cursor, Claude, and whatever comes next), with an informed view of what AI can and can't do today.

We also move fast. Last week we threw a festival for 600 people, planned in under two weeks, with real alpacas on site. That is the energy around here. If that sounds like your kind of chaos, keep reading.
🎯 THE ROLE
We are hiring a UX/UI Designer to own the design of everything a family touches on a screen. That means our marketing website, landing pages, campaign microsites, email, and the whole parent acquisition funnel, plus the product experiences families and providers use once they are in the door. You will work right next to our graphic designer (who owns brand craft and assets) and hand in hand with our product and engineering teams to ship.
Most companies split web and product design across two teams that never talk, so the marketing site and the app end up feeling like two different companies. Not here. You make the entire journey feel like one thing: warm, clear, and a little bit magic. Bold ideas are welcome (an intake that feels like a conversation instead of a form, a landing page that explains autism care to a frightened parent in ten seconds) as long as you can prototype them and ship them.
🚧 WHAT YOU'LL DO
Design and ship our marketing website, landing pages, and campaign microsites
Design email and lifecycle touchpoints that feel human, not corporate
Design the end-to-end journey from first click to booked, and optimize it for clarity and conversion
Run experiments, read the data, and keep reducing friction and time to care
Design family-facing and provider-facing flows, screens, and prototypes, in close partnership with our product team and Founding Product Designer
Turn complex healthcare workflows into interfaces that feel genuinely simple
Create and maintain a design system that spans marketing and product so everything feels like one brand
Prototype fast, test with real parents and BCBAs, and iterate on what you learn
Work directly with engineers to get your designs into production at a high bar, not just into a Figma file
In 90 days: You have shipped a materially better marketing site or set of key landing pages, mapped and improved the top of the acquisition funnel, and laid the foundation of a shared design system with the graphic designer and product team.
In a year: The whole family journey (ad to landing page to intake to app) feels like one seamless product, conversion and time to care have measurably improved, and there's a design system the team builds on every day.
🧠 WHO YOU ARE
You are a self-starter who does not need a PRD to begin. You find the problem and start designing.
You have genuine taste and understand aesthetics, on both the web and product side.
You are a real hybrid: as strong at conversion-driven web and landing pages as you are at product flows, prototypes, and systems.
You are full of bold ideas and pragmatic enough to prototype and ship them on a real deadline.
You are fluent in Figma, comfortable building and maintaining design systems, and you love working with engineers to get things live.
You talk to users and let real insight and data guide your decisions, not just your gut.
You are AI-native and use modern tools to move faster.
You care about families navigating autism care, and it shows in how carefully you design for them.
Front-end familiarity (HTML and CSS, or tools like Framer or Webflow) so you can ship web yourself
Experience with conversion or growth design, or lifecycle and email
